close_reason: Wontfix per workspace AGENTS.md 'Bikeshedding' rule and the parent epic Section 7 calibration ('opinion-labeled forward-major-version flag; close as wontfix unless workspace is planning the next major bump'). The Email::new positional-arg ergonomics issue is a real type-design observation but has no engineering pressure on the current 0.1.x crate. The same shape appears on Mailbox::new (9 positional args + #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]), so any fix would propagate across the canonical-template family. Best addressed in a coordinated breaking-release pass, not piecemeal. Cookie-cutter consistency requires the sibling extension-types crates to mirror Email's shape; reshaping just this one breaks the canonical template. If a major-version bump is planned, file a fresh epic that addresses the positional-arg + Into<Id> generics + per-object id-newtype questions together.
description:
crate-jmap-mail-types/src/email.rs:356-363:

```rust
pub fn new(
    id: Id,
    blob_id: Id,
    thread_id: Id,
    mailbox_ids: HashMap<Id, bool>,
    size: u64,
    received_at: UTCDate,
) -> Self
```

Four `Id`-shaped parameters in positional order. A caller can easily transpose `id` and `blob_id`, or `thread_id` and a mailbox map key, with no compile-time signal — `Id` is `#[serde(transparent)]` over `String`, so the type system treats all four equivalently.

This is the same pattern flagged in the jmap-base-client review under JMAP-6r7c.50 (upload_blob positional args) and JMAP-6r7c.48 (DownloadBlobParams expected_sha256 primitive obsession). Forward-major-version flag.

The fix shape, when this graduates to a major bump, would be either:
- A typed-params struct: `Email::new(params: EmailRequiredFields) -> Self`
- Distinct id newtypes: `EmailId`, `BlobId`, `ThreadId` — though the workspace has historically rejected per-object id newtypes because the JMAP wire treats all ids as opaque strings

The `mailbox_ids: HashMap<Id, bool>` shape is correct for the JMAP wire (object with id-keyed booleans per RFC 8621 §4.1.1) but should not be a positional argument either — it forces every caller to construct the HashMap inline.

Not a present-tense bug. Filed as opinion / forward-major-version flag. Cookie-cutter siblings (Mailbox::new at mailbox.rs:164 takes 9 positional args; `#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]` is already applied) inherit the same shape, so the fix would propagate across the canonical-template family in one pass.
title: Email::new takes six positional arguments (four are bare Id) — primitive obsession at type level
